title: JurisMind — Private legal desk
pitch: A private legal desk in the browser. ChatGPT uses the site’s own WebMCP tools to save holdings with your note and build a support map — only from what you already saved.
about_excerpt: A private legal desk in the browser. ChatGPT uses the site’s own WebMCP tools to save holdings with your note and build a support map — only from what you already saved. Like 1 Comment Story Updates tools maps zero I built JurisMind because I am a lawyer, and I do not want a chatbot inventing case law for me. I also wanted something I can use case by case, not one giant dump of everything I have ever read. The job is simple. I save a source together with why it matters for this case (any case; the demo is just an example). That library lives in my browser, not on a server. That matters because this is where I already work, next to Word and the rest of my case tools. When I ask a question (or when ChatGPT asks it for me), JurisMind builds a "mapa de sustento": excerpt, my note, and the gaps, kept apart. If the library has nothing on that question, it says so. My sources stay organized per case. The rule I actually work with: I decide what enters; the source decides what can be claimed. The UI is in Spanish; I am a lawyer in Colombia, so I built it first for a lawyer who works in Spanish. This page is in English so judges (and you 😅) can read it. Why WebMCP I am not going to paste a whole expediente into a chat window. I am also not going to let an agent invent a back door into my file. WebMCP is the controlled window: the site publishes two tools. ChatGPT can call those tools — review the library, save a holding with my note, build a map — without me uploading the case to someone else’s server. The page stays the source of truth. (A browser agent can still see what is on screen; WebMCP is not magic privacy. It is an honest tool access.) What we can do together now I open https://jurismind-five.vercel.app . ChatGPT looks at the origin and finds the real tools — capturar_recurso and buscar_y_armar . It does not invent an API. Then, in ordinary language (the demo is caso Ramírez: high-cost medicine, EPS delay): it reviews what is already in mi biblioteca it finds an official Corte Constitucional judgment, opens it, and saves it with my note it builds the map only from what is saved — and it flags when a card matches the note but has no excerpt yet I ask something the library cannot support ( caducidad de la reparación directa ) and I get 0 fuentes . No invented sentencia. That is the feature. 🙂 Before this, either I clicked the UI myself or I hoped the model would not hallucinate the rest. Those were the options. How it is wired document.modelContext.registerTool on this origin only. capturar_recurso — write. Needs url and nota . Optional title, excerpt, collection. buscar_y_armar — read. Needs query . Opens the map in the page. IndexedDB per origin. Production and localhost are not the same library. No case-file backend. Chrome production has a WebMCP origin trial. ChatGPT Desktop works with Sol or Terra (not Luna). Gemini Nano / Prompt API can classify if the device has it; there is a fallback that does not depend on it. Repo: https://github.com/cristianbdev/jurismind (MIT). Video: https://youtu.be/2MnIFDTDRkE Test it like a lawyer, and you'll see what I see Open the live URL in ChatGPT Desktop. Optional: “Probar el caso Ramírez” loads three official Colombian sources you can delete. Then talk to ChatGPT the way you would talk to a junior: look at the file, go get a sentencia, save it with a note, arm the argument, then ask something that should come back empty. I made JurisMind end to end for this Challenge: the local library, the mapa de sustento, the two WebMCP tools (capturar_recurso and buscar_y_armar), the ChatGPT Desktop demo, and the submission. I want tools that other lawyers can trust and use!
